notes.s: Two members sing the story of their own friendship, to each other.
notes.t: Jimin and V, both born in 1995, both moved to Seoul as teenagers to train, and this is the only song in the catalogue where two members narrate how they met and what it cost. The first verse is one of them describing the other as an alien he could not read; the second swaps to V naming Jimin out loud and counting seven years. The dumpling incident and the bus home from school are real shared history rather than imagery, which is why fan reaction to the song was so disproportionate to its position as an album track. The chorus asks for the friendship to outlast the noise, not the career.
k: 하루는 A 하루는 B is the frame for one day this, the next day that. 웬수 is a deliberate misspelling of 원수, a sworn enemy or blood foe, and in the misspelt form it is what Koreans call family and close friends they cannot get along with or without. Translating it as enemy loses the affection.

Promises in Korea are sealed by hooking little fingers, often with thumbs stamped on top. The pinky is not an anatomical detail, it is the promise itself, which is why the next lines measure time against promises.

An in-joke the fandom can date and a translation cannot carry: a trainee-era argument over dumplings that the two of them have retold on camera. Korean uses 사건, incident or case, for this kind of private legend the way English says the great whatever.
Standard spelling is 한결같아, meaning constant throughout. Stretching the final 아 to 애 is a lyric and texting habit that reads as warm and spoken rather than careless.

vocab.note: 땀에 배다, to be soaked in sweat, is the set phrase

vocab.en: to be strange, to be off
vocab.note: Covers both odd and wrong, as in 뭔가 이상해, something's not right
Also used for an issue still waiting to be solved
The lyric spells it 웬수, the colloquial form used half-fondly for family and close friends

vocab.en: cheering, a roar from a crowd
vocab.note: Specifically the sound of many people shouting at once, as in a stadium
Used of rain, bleeding, sound; people and vehicles 멈추다 instead
새끼 is the young of an animal, so this is the baby finger; 엄지 is the thumb

vocab.en: memory you look back on fondly
vocab.note: 기억 is the act of remembering; 추억 is the keepsake
Also what you call plans with someone, 약속 있어요
Pairs with 등교, going to school; both nouns take 하다
Praise for a person who stays the same through everything
Mildly dismissive; 뻔한 영화 is a film you can see coming
